acts.name: Fun and its quiet price (loneliness, ageing)
The slide: revenge, theft, heist, the choice not to save
Bigger world: you are last episode's villain; cliffhanger; CTA

loops.what: Rule 3 (your frozen minutes are real) -> you age an extra ~2 weeks a year; mom notices you look tired
Narrator wink that nobody promised you were a hero -> full villain slide
Saving a kid's ice cream ('best thing you ever did') -> not saving a whole crashing car
Fear of being alone in frozen time forever -> someone else is moving in frozen time
Best friend's doubt -> he asks if it was you on the news; you lie; he stops texting
Previous episode's unreadable villain on a stopped highway -> it was you; the speedster from ep 1 is in the lineup
Gray-coat woman is not frozen -> who is she? (Shapeshift episode pays it off)

beats.summary: Mid-laugh at lunch you knock over your drink and it hangs in the air; the whole cafeteria is frozen except you. You poke it, scoop it back into the cup.
Time resumes; your friend finishes his story and is confused that the spill never happened.
Title question verbatim + 'here's how it works'.
visual: title card over in-world wall clock

beats.summary: Teaser ('something weird first'): the brain already stretches time when your eyes jump to a clock; a named, tested illusion.
Satellite clocks drift by microseconds per day; uncorrected, your phone map would be off by kilometres daily. Big consequence from a tiny number.
visual: navy card 38 MICROSECONDS satellite vs house clocks

beats.summary: Animals perceive time differently: a fly sees flicker several times faster, so your swatting hand is slow motion to it.
But a true stop would break you three ways: no light reaches your eyes, no sound moves, and frozen air traps you like a wall.
Rule 1: a small bubble of normal air and light travels with you.
Rule 2: what you hold moves, what you let go of freezes. Basketball left hanging over the hoop; walking home through frozen rain soaks you; mom is baffled.
Rule 3: frozen minutes are real minutes of your life. You test it with a book, a pizza and a nap; the clock hasn't moved but your body has. You decide to just not overdo it.
Demo for the best friend: you appear across the room. He names the anime power he thinks it is.
Perk montage that slides into cheating: queue-skipping, a gross sneeze aside, copying test answers. Narrator winks that you were never promised to be the hero. The teacher becomes suspicious.
Extra sleep every morning; nudging the goalie a step before a penalty; secretly saving a little kid's ice cream, flagged as the best use of the power.
Prank: mom's coffee mug turns up somewhere absurd every morning.
The frozen world described as a place: no wind, birds hung on strings, lying down on a highway and in a mall; the quietest, loneliest place there is.
Rule 3 adds up: an hour a day equals about two extra weeks a year that only you lived. Mom says you look tired. At night: what if time never restarts?
Public humiliation by a bully; for the first time you use the power for payback: tied laces, phone in the fish tank. It feels great, because nobody can ever know.

Theft ladder: snack, then shoes, then a phone from a locked case. You keep a list of what you could take. Frozen cameras make footage skip. Hood up. Your best friend asks if it's bad stuff; you deflect.
Friend looks a beat too long, laughs it off, never asks to see the trick again.
The heist: weekly cash truck, you on the overpass in your hood, freeze. A neighbouring car is mid-crash with its tyre in the air and a terrified driver.
You could fix the crash in minutes, but you came for the truck. Direct callback to the ice cream you once saved.
You choose the money, let time go, hear the crash behind you. Nobody badly hurt; all the camera shows is a faceless hooded figure.
In bed you rewatch the footage, feel untouchable rather than guilty. Best friend texts asking if it was you; you type 'no'; he goes silent. Someone else is watching the same footage.
Next morning the team waits outside. Roll call of costumes, including the speedster from the last episode. The mind-reader can't read you, which explains the previous cliffhanger. Nervous banter.
You freeze them all, stroll between them, flick the floating can. Nobody can stop you.
In a world where nothing moves, someone says your name: the gray-coat woman, standing behind you, not frozen.
What would you do + join the organisation or fight them; series sign-off.
